subject: Energy
title: Reprocessing Spent Fuel
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Reprocessing Spent Fuel.

hook.text: Spent fuel still contains 96% usable material—reprocessing extracts uranium and plutonium for new fuel.

buildup.text: France reprocesses most of its spent fuel at La Hague—recycling plutonium into MOX fuel for reactors.

discovery.text: Reprocessing reduces waste volume and toxicity—the remaining waste decays to background levels in about 300 years.

twist.text: The US banned civilian reprocessing in 1977—fearing that separated plutonium could be diverted for weapons.

climax.text: The debate continues: reprocessing reduces waste but creates proliferation risk—there's no easy answer.

punchline.text: Recycle the fuel or bury it all—each path has costs.

quiz.question: Why did the US ban civilian reprocessing?
